body: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals is a Japanese role-playing game about Maxim and the companions who join his struggle against the Sinistrals. Released on the Super Nintendo, it takes place ninety-nine years before the first Lufia. That position gives the adventure a particular weight: it explores the people behind a history already introduced to players. Towns and turn-based battles supply a familiar framework, while the dungeons ask for observation and manipulation of the environment as well as a strong party.

Inside a dungeon, enemies are visible and respond to Maxim’s movement. Waiting gives the player time to consider a route; taking a step advances the situation. Tools such as arrows, bombs and a hookshot extend that relationship with the environment. An object may be part of a puzzle, a route may need opening, and a monster may be avoided or temporarily stopped. The result gives exploration its own decisions between battles, rather than treating every corridor as a pause before the next encounter.

Equipment does more than increase statistics. Its IP abilities use a gauge built through taking damage, giving an older piece of gear a reason to remain useful after a stronger replacement appears. Capsule Monsters add another companion: these creatures fight under their own control and can develop when fed items or equipment. Together, these systems make preparation less automatic. The party’s strength comes from the tools and abilities it retains, and the player has to decide which combinations are worth carrying into the next dungeon.
